question: Why do IQ tests keep being rescored?
answer: Because raw scores kept rising — roughly three points a decade through the 20th century, across many countries. Tests are re-normed to keep the average at 100, which hides the drift. Score as an average adult today and you would have sat near the top of the distribution a century ago.
move: The average is held at 100 by moving the goalposts every few years.
